## Result: a candidate theorem package for collective thermal bound entanglement

The strongest outcome is a family of quantum states that can be generated from a completely unentangled, maximally mixed input by ideal collective thermalization, yet exhibit an unusual combination:

**Every one-qubit-versus-rest partition is separable, while the whole state becomes almost maximally distinguishable from every fully separable state.**

I developed this into all-size arguments, a local-measurement certification principle, quantitative entanglement bounds, finite-time preparation guarantees, and an **executed exact-rational four-qubit certificate**.

This is an internally derived research result, **not an independently verified field-breaking discovery**. Correctness and priority still require specialist review. The literature and repository checks identified substantial prior work that must not be presented as new.

**Deliverables:** RESEARCH_NOTE.pdf[12-page derivation and proof note](sandbox:/mnt/data/astra_thermal_bound_entanglement/RESEARCH_NOTE.pdf) · astra_thermal_bound_entanglement.zip[Complete reproducible packet](sandbox:/mnt/data/astra_thermal_bound_entanglement.zip) · certify_finite_time.py[Exact-rational certificate script](sandbox:/mnt/data/astra_thermal_bound_entanglement/certify_finite_time.py)

## 1. The main mathematical result

Consider \(N\) qubits with collective spin operators
\[
J_a=\frac12\sum_{i=1}^{N}\sigma_a^{(i)}.
\]
Start with
\[
\rho(0)=\frac{I}{2^N}
\]
and evolve under
\[
\frac{d\rho}{dt}
=
\Gamma\left[(\nu+1)\mathcal D[J_-]+\nu\mathcal D[J_+]\right](\rho),
\]
where
\[
\mathcal D[L](\rho)
=
L\rho L^\dagger-\frac12\{L^\dagger L,\rho\}.
\]

Here \(\nu>0\) is the bath occupation at the transition frequency. The model assumes **uniform collective coupling**, with no additional local noise or drive during preparation. This collective thermal master equation, including entanglement generation from maximally mixed two-qubit inputs, already appears in Li–Xu’s work. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/pdf/quant-ph/0505216)

Let \(\rho_N\) be the stationary state selected by this particular initial condition. The candidate theorem package establishes the following.

### Exact separation across every singleton cut

For every \(N\ge2\),
\[
\boxed{
\rho_N\text{ is separable across every }1|(N-1)\text{ cut}
\iff
\nu\ge \nu_*:=\frac{\sqrt{15}-3}{6}.
}
\]

Research state dated 8 October 2026. All advances are internally derived candidates, not externally reviewed or priority-cleared results. No independent subagents were available.

Strict-interior occupations admit actual finite-time singleton-PPT, strongly non-fully-separable states at conservative O_nu(N)/Gamma time under unnormalized jumps. Group distillation needs specified joint operations and charged postselection.

# Audit update and preparation-time escalation

8 October 2026. Read this BEFORE RESULT_AND_RESTART.md. Status: internally derived candidate mathematics, not external peer review, proof-assistant certification, or priority clearance. No independent subagents were available.

This file supersedes the old checkpoint's execution counts, hashes, missing-code reference, and unresolved preparation-time statement. The earlier stationary-state and anti-concentration arguments remain candidate proofs. Current portable exact code: certify_finite_time.py in this directory.

## 1. Prior-art and prior-capital corrections

Li and Xu, arXiv:quant-ph/0505216v2, already give the SAME collective thermal generator, stationary two-qubit formulas, and threshold nu_*=(sqrt(15)-3)/6. See Eq. (1), Eqs. (10)-(11), and p. 3, including their explicitly discussed initially maximally mixed case r=0. Their symbol N is bath occupation, not our number of qubits. Submitted 2005; International Journal of Quantum Information 6,1165 (2008). The numerical constant and basic bath-induced entanglement are NOT new.

A final repository refresh found AA/N120, cards/N120-thermal-depth-two.txt, blob 4eddcc744a068d497456b4ad166bae33801864e3. It already records ideal thermal activation, a finite-time entanglement bound via a reflecting-chain spectral-gap comparison, stationary pair decompositions, and a stronger source-reported all-time depth-two result. Thus neither basic finite-time thermal entanglement nor the birth-death comparison strategy is claimed new. The added finite-time conclusion here is an explicit singleton-PPT margin combined with asymptotically strong separation from full separability. N120's all-time depth statement was not independently certified by our finite-time code. The refreshed 01_CORE.txt blob was 4f84ffebb34d7724e0d6c07ffbbb4ff0c554e282; the earlier start/core snapshot in RESULT_AND_RESTART.md is historical provenance, not the current repository state.

Candidate contributions requiring specialist priority review: the all-size singleton-separability/PPT extension; the reusable common-axis LOCC anti-concentration bound; full-separability distance tending to one; the regularized-relative-entropy lower bound with arbitrary local cross-copy correlations; and the combined finite-time PPT preparation/group-distillation interface. These are not claimed as established historical firs
